title: Entity routing safety and write-fencing playbook
content:
Purpose:

This note captures a practical playbook for the control plane data model and CRUD APIs with a strong emphasis on safe routing and write-fencing across regions and clusters. The goal is to reduce cross-region write conflicts, make routing predictable, and provide clear operator tooling for recovery and reconciliation. This is intentionally implementation-agnostic but concrete enough to guide API contracts and the runtime behavior for the control plane.

Design goals (prioritized):
- Safety first: prevent silent divergence from concurrent writes and avoid split-brain configuration state.
- Low-latency reads: route reads locally when safe to do so.
- Predictable writes: explicit ownership/leases for write operations to bound fanout.
- Idempotency and reconciliation: all user-facing writes must be idempotent and reconciler-friendly.
- Clear operator actions: provide admin APIs for forced takeovers, fencing, and reconciliation with strong audit trails.

High-level model overview:
- Resources: opaque domain objects (ModelVariant, Route, Deployment, ClusterBinding, TenantConfig). Each resource has a stable resource_id (UUID-like), a resource_type, and a version token (monotonic integer).
- Environments: logical grouping (dev, staging, prod) that scopes visibility/route policies.
- Regions: physical cloud regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1) used for routing affinity and capacity.
- Clusters: runtime clusters inside a region; clusters are the targets of mechanical routing and hold local leases for resource ownership.

Record canonical fields (per resource):
- resource_id: string (stable identifier)
- resource_type: string
- environment: string
- region_affinity: list of regions (primary, secondary, allowed_fallbacks)
- cluster_binding: string (cluster id) or null if unbound
- version: string (opaque incrementing token, e.g., v23 or monotonic int serialized)
- last_modified_by: string (actor id)
- last_modified_at: ISO8601 timestamp
- tombstone: boolean (soft-delete marker)
- lease: optional {holder: cluster-id, lease_expires_at: ISO8601, lease_token: string} (see leasing below)
- metadata: freeform map stored as JSON blob (note: stored as a string in documents)

Important: in the Drive docs we represent metadata as opaque JSON strings for compatibility with existing readers.

ID strategy and aliasing:
- resource_id must be stable and globally unique. Prefer UUIDv4 or k-sorted UUID for index performance.
- Canonical name (human friendly) is a separate indexed field and can change; canonical names are not authoritative for ownership.
- Allow stable external aliases (e.g., external_id) for cross-system reconciliation; keep a simple many->one alias index to avoid accidental duplicates.

Region and cluster affinity semantics:
- region_affinity.primary: one preferred region where the resource is expected to be active.
- region_affinity.secondary: 0..N regions that may accept writes only when explicitly allowed (see Fencing).
- cluster_binding: when set, the cluster is expected to hold a local lease for muted writes. Use cluster_binding only when the resource is pinned for operational reasons (SLA, isolation).

Routing policies (read and write):
- Read routing: default is serve-from-local-region if the local record version >= last_known_version_for_client. If local is older, either forward-read to primary region or return a staleness indicator and a suggested re-try.
- Write routing (default): route writes to primary region (region_affinity.primary). If a client connects to a non-primary region, the control plane will either proxy to primary or perform a write with explicit cross-region fencing if the client supplies a valid takeover token.
- Read-after-write: API returns resulting version and last_modified_at so clients can verify local visibility.

Write-fencing and leases (core safety mechanism):
- Lease model: clusters can acquire exclusive write leases for a resource for a bounded TTL. Lease acquisition returns a lease_token and lease_expires_at.
- Lease acquisition is conditional: requires presenting the resource version you are upgrading from (optimistic). Successful acquisition bumps an internal owner_version and issues a lease_token.
- Fencing token: any volume of writes that must be serialized across regions must include either the active lease_token or a server-validated takeover token (issued by operators via admin API).
- Takeover flow: operator requests takeover -> control plane issues a time-limited takeover_token -> clients performing takeover writes must include takeover_token and new owner info -> system records an audit entry and invalidates competing leases.

Idempotency and conflict handling:
- API surface must accept an idempotency_key on mutating requests. Replays within a configurable window (e.g., 24h) return the same result.
- Updates include if-match: version token. If if-match mismatches, return HTTP 409 with a canonical conflict object describing current version and a suggested merge path.
- Merges: for complex resources, provide server-side merge semantics (three-way merge based on last_write, base_version, and patch). Keep merge deterministic and documented per resource type.

CRUD API surface (examples and conventions):
- POST /v1/resources -> create new resource
  - body: {resource_type, environment, canonical_name?, metadata, region_affinity?}  -> returns {resource_id, version, lease: null}
- GET /v1/resources/{resource_id}?region=eu-west-1 -> get resource from requested region (may be local or proxied).
- PATCH /v1/resources/{resource_id} -> partial update; requires if-match and supports idempotency_key and optional lease_token.
  - body: {patch: JSONPatch, if_match: "v23", idempotency_key: "x"} -> returns {resource_id, version, lease}
- DELETE /v1/resources/{resource_id} -> soft-delete (set tombstone=true, keep for GC window) requires operator_confirm=true for resources bound to clusters or production environment.
- POST /v1/resources/{resource_id}/lease -> attempt to acquire lease: {holder: cluster-id, if_match: "v23", requested_ttl_seconds: 30} -> returns {lease_token, lease_expires_at, owner_version}
- POST /v1/resources/{resource_id}/takeover -> operator-only: {reason, operator_id, force: boolean} -> returns {takeover_token, valid_until}
- GET /v1/resources?environment=prod&region=us-west-2&type=Route -> list with pagination and last_seen_version metadata.

Error model and safety codes (suggested):
- 400: Bad Request (invalid payload)
- 401: Unauthorized
- 403: Forbidden (admin-only action)
- 404: Not Found
- 409: Conflict (version mismatch) -> include conflict.payload: {current_version, diff_hint}
- 423: Locked (resource is leased by another cluster) -> include lease details and estimated ETA or takeover_token link
- 425: Too Early (stale-read suggested) -> includes a suggested forward location or re-check window
- 429: Rate limit
- 500: Internal Error with reconciler ticket id for operator follow-up

Reconciliation and eventual consistency patterns:
- Event-log (append-only) per resource is strongly recommended for audit and reconciliation. Each write emits an event with (actor, op, base_version, resulting_version, region, lease_token?).
- Background reconciler: periodically compares local state with authoritative global state (or leader region). Reconciler must be able to perform non-destructive merges or create tickets for operator manual resolution.
- GC and tombstones: keep tombstones for at least 7 days for safety; after GC window, hard delete. Provide admin endpoints for immediate purge under strict audit.

Operational admin tooling and workflows:
- Force takeover: admin calls /takeover to get takeover_token, then submits write with takeover_token; control plane logs audit and sends event to reconciler to scrub stale leases.
- Lease diagnostics: /admin/leases?resource_id=... returns history and current holder.
- Reconciliation UI: show divergent versions across regions, diff of key fields, and one-click accept/merge with audit log.
- Emergency read-only mode: operator can flip environment to read-only which auto-rejects writes with a clear HTTP 403 and suggested migration path.

Migration and cross-region deployment notes:
- When enabling a new region as primary for a subset of resources, perform a controlled handoff: 1) ensure data sync completed, 2) acquire leases in old primary and new primary sequentially, 3) issue takeover_token and switch region_affinity.primary under an operator transaction.
- Prefer blue/green rollouts for schema changes in metadata blob shapes; keep backward-compatible readers and provide translation helpers in runtime.

Examples (flow):
- Normal update in primary region:
  1) client PATCH with if-match="v34" -> control plane validates, increments to v35, writes event v35, returns v35.
- Client connected to non-primary (local stale):
  1) client PATCH without lease_token -> control plane responds 409 or 423 depending on staleness, with guidance: proxy=true to primary or request takeover.
- Cluster takeover due to failover:
  1) operator requests takeover -> control plane issues takeover_token valid 30s -> new cluster submits PATCH with takeover_token -> control plane logs event, sets lease_token, invalidates previous leases, returns new version.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Strict single-writer-per-resource vs. per-field commuting writes: do we allow per-field CRDT-style merges for low-risk fields (metadata) while enforcing single-writer for critical binding fields (cluster_binding, region_affinity)?
- Lease TTL sizing: short TTL reduces stale ownership window but increases refresh churn; long TTL reduces churn but increases takeover latency. Consider dynamic TTLs per resource type or autoscaling TTLs based on access patterns.
- Event store retention: how much history to keep on disk vs cold storage? Longer retention helps debugging but increases storage cost.

Audit and observability requirements:
- Emit structured events for every mutation (actor, token, base_version, result_version, region).
- Metrics: lease acquisition latency/failure rate, takeover occurrences, cross-region proxy rate, reconcile actions per hour, tombstone purge rate.
- Tracing: attach request-id and region hop metadata to cross-region proxied requests.

Appendix: small-term checklist for engineering owners:
- [ ] Implement if-match in all PATCH endpoints
- [ ] Add lease acquisition API and server-side validation
- [ ] Add takeover admin API and token issuance
- [ ] Add structured event emission for every write
- [ ] Add reconciliation job and a dashboard showing divergence
- [ ] Document operator runbook for forced takeovers and GC

This doc is intentionally prescriptive — use it as a starting point for API spec PRs and early runtime prototypes. The next step is to convert key flows into a machine-readable OpenAPI draft and a short integration PoC between control-plane and two-region runtime to validate latency and takeover safety.
